clue.text: Initiates approaches to restrain old boys' clubs

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: someone who approaches comes near
old boys, grown up, are men
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A man takes on the stuffy gentlemen's clubs, making overtures to rein them in.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to begin or start it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Write badly without direction and make slow progress

indicators.note: without means the next piece is left out of the word before it

parts.note: to scrawl is to write untidily
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Poor handwriting and no sense of where it is going: a writer stuck in a rut.
explanation.definitionFit: To move along at a snail's pace, like a baby on all fours, is a synonym for slow progress.

clue.text: Clue for a TV show where beer is made

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the first word is an anagram signal and the second its fodder, giving the letters A TV, so the answer is a clue for those words; the first word is also a TV show's title

explanation.surface: A quiz setter wants a hint for a television programme set in a brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, says shuffle the letters of a vat to get A TV, so it is a clue for 'a TV'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewers steep malt in hot water in a large tub to make wort, the first stage of brewing.

clue.text: Enlist boy soldier, the last to be replaced by noon

indicators.note: to be replaced by means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: Errol is a boy's name, as in Errol Flynn

indicators.note: the last picks the final letter of soldier

explanation.surface: A lad joins up as a boy soldier, though the final man is swapped at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up or join a list, such as the army roll, is a synonym for enlisting.

clue.text: Boy and girl turned up sick inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the other

parts.note: someone who turned up arrived, or came
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A boy and girl arrived, but were feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like a reversal signal but means arrived. The name is given to both sexes in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is borne by both men (Camille Saint-Saëns) and women (Camille Claudel), so it fits either.

clue.text: Sour spice used in and around Lent

indicators.note: the letters are used in and around each other, mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A tart flavouring is cooked with during the Lenten season.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic means bad-tempered and spiteful, a sour disposition.

clue.text: Girl one met at a party

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A man recalls a girl he once met at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive celebration or special social occasion is a synonym for a party.

clue.text: Boy said to be heathen?

indicators.note: said to be means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a heathen is without a god, so jokingly free of one

explanation.surface: Is a certain lad reputed to be a pagan?
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional male first name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Middle of single bed that is badly askew, in which one gets no sleep

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the two words taken together
in which means a piece goes inside the jumbled letters
badly means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: A single bed that is badly askew keeps its occupant tossing all night.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'single bed', taken as nine letters, is L. 'Badly' jumbles ASKEW into SWAKE, and 'in which' puts A inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain conscious in bed through the night is an idiom for failing to get any rest.

clue.text: It's part of a kit of beer supplied to Germany with chaser

parts.note: Bass is a well-known brand of British beer
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a chaser is a spirit drunk after beer, such as rum

explanation.surface: A beer delivered to Germany, with a shot to follow, comes as part of a kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum kit includes a large low drum played with a pedal, so it is one part of it.

clue.text: Boy initiated and carried out some spooning

parts.note: a lad is a boy
someone who initiated something led it

explanation.surface: A young man made the first move and did some cuddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooning' suggests courting, but here it means serving with a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve soup with a large spoon is to do some spooning, literally.

clue.text: Qualification shows everything about a girl

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: everything means all
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A certificate reveals all there is to know about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: An A level is the English school-leaving exam taken at eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: An A level is an academic qualification, an exam pass in one subject at the end of school.

clue.text: Girl, star at last in Crazy Lady for about four weeks

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the jumbled letters
crazy means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of star

explanation.surface: A young woman becomes the star of a mad stage show for a month's run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges the four letters to L...DAY, leaving room after the L for the girl and the star's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar month, from new moon to new moon, lasts roughly twenty-nine and a half days, nearly four weeks.

clue.text: New boy?

definitions.meaning: something that has only just arrived is fresh or recent

explanation.surface: A fresh arrival at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the phrase means only recently arrived; as one word it is a boy's name.

clue.text: Cheerful Boatman's a mischievous chap, prone to compileritis?

parts.note: up means cheerful or in good spirits
Boatman is the setter, who refers to himself impersonally as one, so his is one's
an elf is a mischievous little fellow

explanation.surface: The setter cheerfully admits to being an impish fellow who is prone to setter's vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up oneself' is British slang for conceited. 'Compileritis' is a made-up ailment of crossword compilers.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means smug and self-important, the setter's joke ailment of vanity being an invented example.

clue.text: Unpleasant sensations, lacking love

indicators.note: unpleasant suggests the letters are made disagreeable, mixed up

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so it means O

explanation.surface: Feelings that turn nasty once affection has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O out of SENSATIONS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and unpleasantness, felt where there is no love, describe the noun well.

clue.text: Ashdown's May forfeit at end of vote: a myth? Not exactly, at last

indicators.note: last means this piece goes at the very end
end of picks the final letter of vote
not exactly means the letters are not in their exact order

explanation.surface: Paddy Ashdown's famous bet about the election poll: was it a myth?
explanation.walkthrough: In May 2015 former Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown promised on TV to eat his hat if the exit poll was right; it was.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is the rash wager one offers to forfeit, which Ashdown made over the May exit poll.

clue.text: It's sweet girl in some trouble

indicators.note: in means one piece goes within the other
trouble means the letters are disturbed

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A sweet young woman finds herself in a spot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' is the anagram signal, turning the fodder into MOES, not the definition it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle-like syrup left from sugar refining is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Two-part choral work has no place for heartless imp of a boy

indicators.note: has no place for means a piece is left out

parts.note: antiphony is singing by two choirs answering each other

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A choir piece leaves no room for a cruel little rascal of a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless imp' is IP, which comes out of the choral word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common male first name, so an example of a boy.

clue.text: Subdues partner's boy

definitions.meaning: as two words, treads on or crushes
a son of one's spouse from an earlier relationship

explanation.surface: A man keeps his partner's son in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means crushes underfoot; as one, the son of one's spouse.

clue.text: Girl auto enthusiasts?

parts.note: an auto is a car
men here are the fans, as in car men

explanation.surface: A young woman who loves cars.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's name, best known from Bizet's opera heroine.

clue.text: Hairnet girl used for curling

indicators.note: curling means the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl wears a hairnet for setting her curls.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is the end of 'Hairnet' plus 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spiral lock of hair is an example of hair styled into curls.

clue.text: Girl to excel with food

parts.note: to beat is to excel or outdo
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A young woman who outdoes everyone at cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's name, as in Shakespeare's heroine in Much Ado.

clue.text: Isn't able to get girl into bed

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man fails to get his date to go to bed with him.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the negative of can, meaning lacks the ability.

clue.text: Screw as a boy, perhaps eaten by lion?

indicators.note: eaten by means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
a boy is an example of a male, he

explanation.surface: A boy is devoured by a lion, as if in a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw someone in slang is to swindle them, a synonym for cheat.

clue.text: This animal under study could lead to grass

indicators.note: the study placed before the animal could lead to the word for grass, so taking the study away leaves the animal

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, to denounce
a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: An animal under scrutiny might end up turning to grass for food.
explanation.walkthrough: Put DEN (study) above the answer and you get the verb for grass; 'under' says the animal comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard of Central Asia is also called by this name, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Boatman in Paris (capital!) to find a boy

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, I, and in French I is je
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: The setter goes to the French capital in search of a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Jerome K. Jerome, whose Three Men in a Boat suits a setter called Boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boy's name, as borne by the author of Three Men in a Boat.

clue.text: Girl sent crazy by LSD in the '60s

indicators.note: crazy means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A girl tripping on acid in the swinging sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD was the abbreviation for pounds, shillings and pence, British money before decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: British currency, pounds shillings and pence, was abbreviated LSD before the decimal switch.

clue.text: Imperfect, flawed, failing you fundamentally?

indicators.note: fundamentally points to the base or first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A list of damning faults in someone's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious or of uncertain quality is a fair summary of imperfect and flawed.

clue.text: Perhaps my girl's only starting letting loose

parts.note: the apostrophe s gives the letter S

indicators.note: starting picks the first letter of only
letting loose means the letters are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's girlfriend is just beginning to let herself go.
explanation.walkthrough: My Girl is a song by the Temptations, so its name is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: My Girl is the name of a Temptations song, an example of what the phrase describes.
